facts.statement: Albertochampsa was named in 1972 by the researcher Bruce Erickson.
facts.quote: It was named in 1972 by Bruce Erickson

facts.statement: The type species of the genus is Albertochampsa langstoni.
facts.quote: the type species is A. langstoni

facts.statement: Albertochampsa lived in Alberta during the Late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: from the Late Cretaceous of Alberta

facts.statement: Fossils of Albertochampsa come from the Campanian-age Dinosaur Park Formation.
facts.quote: It is known from a skull from the Campanian-age Dinosaur Park Formation

facts.statement: Albertochampsa was a rare find in the Dinosaur Park Formation.
The skull of Albertochampsa measured approximately 21 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: The skull of Albertochampsa was only about 21 cm long (8.3 in)

facts.statement: Albertochampsa is classified as an extinct alligatorid, possibly representing a stem-caiman or a basal alligatorine.
facts.quote: an extinct genus of alligatorid (possibly a stem-caiman or a basal alligatorine)

facts.statement: Albertochampsa belongs to the family Alligatoridae.
facts.quote: Albertochampsa is a member of the family Alligatoridae

facts.statement: Scientists debate whether Albertochampsa is more closely related to modern alligators or caimans.
facts.quote: although it is disputed whether Albertochampsa is more closely related to the alligators or the caimans

facts.statement: A 2018 study placed Albertochampsa as more closely related to caimans within the subfamily Caimaninae.
facts.quote: The below cladogram from a 2018 study shows Albertochampsa as more closely related to the caimans in the subfamily Caimaninae

facts.statement: A 2022 analysis by Walter et al. recovered Albertochampsa as one of the most basal alligatorines.
facts.quote: Walter et al. (2022) recovered them as the basalmost alligatorines based on phylogenetic analysis

facts.statement: Albertochampsa lived between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago during the Campanian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)
